source.title: Two sisters with Rett syndrome and non-identical paternally-derived microdeletions in the MECP2 gene.

accessException.reason: Publisher copyright ("© Springer Science+Business Media B.V. 2008"); not in the PMC open-access set and no Creative Commons licence. Free to read on PMC only. Europe PMC metadata lists the licence as "cc by", but the PMC record carries only the publisher copyright, so that claim is not relied on.
accessException.decision: Kept in the held-out split: the held-out set is defined as the 10 T33 cases and has already been scored once, so replacing the case would rewrite the evaluation history. Flagged as an exception to the open-access requirement.
accessException.use: Only short quotes (at most 30 words) for verification and a paraphrased note; article text is not stored in the repository or redistributed.

confirmation.summary: Novel 18 bp MECP2 deletion c.1155_1172del18 in Case 1, with symptoms of RTT.
evidence: Sequencing of the MECP2 gene in Case 1 revealed a novel 18 base-pair (bp) deletion, c.1155_1172del18

note.text: My daughter fed poorly as a baby, although feeding improved after we switched to a bottle. By seven months she seemed unusually floppy, paid less attention to things around her and her head was growing more slowly. She began having frightening episodes after waking up and would repeatedly bang on the table. She never managed to sit steadily on her own. She has never spoken recognizable words, and her development has worried us for a long time.
note.author: T33 hand-off (assistant-written from the article; not the parent's words)

uncertainty: The article is not open-access licensed (see source.accessException), and NCBI does not allow automated full-text download. Quotes were checked by reading the public PMC page on 2026-10-24 and cannot be re-checked by verify-sources.
